paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. A family can get a promise from God and then try to rush it along with a plan of its own. Rebekah's plan had a disguise, a dish and a lie, and Jacob said "I am Esau, your firstborn" (Genesis 27:19). The passage shows us how far people will go when they decide God needs their help.

And look at what it cost. Isaac "began to tremble violently" (Genesis 27:33), and Esau "let out a loud and bitter cry" (Genesis 27:34). Isaac said, "Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing" (Genesis 27:35). I think this is the heavy part of the lesson: a shortcut can get you what you wanted and still leave a whole family hurting. Jacob got the blessing his father spoke over him, and he walked out of that tent with a brother who was crying.

Now hold on to this, because the story isn't over. Isaac told Esau, "But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck" (Genesis 27:40), so the last word on this family hasn't been spoken. I'm not going to tell you what comes next, baker. I'll just say that when you're tempted to bake the batch early because the oven feels slow, remember this one. Waiting is hard, and I know that better than most, because I did a lot of it in the back of a drawer.
